newsitem.title: GERMANY: Germany's Rexrodt sees EU deal in January on VW.
newsitem.headline: Germany's Rexrodt sees EU deal in January on VW.

text.p: German Economics Minister Guenter Rexrodt said on Friday he was confident of reaching a resolution next month to Bonn's dispute with the European Commission over state aid for car maker Volkswagen AG.
Germany and Brussels have been at odds over aid given to Volkswagen by east German Saxony state in violation of a ruling by the Commission that forbid some of the aid from being paid.
"In the case of VW and Saxony all parties have showed satisfactory flexibility," Rexrodt told a news conference in Bonn. "I am confident we will reach an agreement in January."
Questioned further by reporters, Rexrodt would only say that one compromise might require additional investment in east Germany, but he would not elaborate.

Earlier this week, EU Competition Commissioner Karel Van Miert told a German newspaper he was ready to allow the payment of some 240 million marks ($154.1 million) in aid to Volkswagen under certain conditions.
This would include greater investment by VW elsewhere in east Germany or the reduction of capacity at other VW plants, which Van Miert described as "probably not the best solution".
-- William Boston, Bonn Newsroom, 49 228 2609750 ($ = 1.557 German Marks)
